key_insight: Self-powered microsystems need more than better harvesters: the biggest barrier is now end-to-end integration of diverse ambient energy sources with ultra-low-power management and storage.
engineering_relevance: The review points engineers toward system-level design choices that enable battery-independent IoT, wearables, and embedded sensing under real-world operating conditions.
method: Surveyed major harvesting modalities: TENGs, piezoelectric/pyroelectric devices, indoor photovoltaics, RF rectennas, and hybrid systems.
Compared materials advances with power-management constraints such as cold-start PMICs, impedance matching, and storage degradation.
Highlighted newer approaches including liquid-solid TENGs, nonlinear piezoelectric oscillators, ML-guided materials discovery, and metamaterial RF harvesters.
evidence_signal: The abstract cites reported gains such as over 300% broader bandwidth for nonlinear piezoelectric oscillators and improved RF harvesting via multiband/broadband metamaterial architectures.
watch_item: Promising harvesting materials can still fail in practice if cold-start power, hybrid source matching, and long-term storage reliability are not addressed together.
paper_title: Energy Harvesting for Self-Powered Microsystems: A Critical Review of Materials, Power Management, and System Integration
